newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian copper recovers, other base metals subdued.
newsitem.headline: Indian copper recovers, other base metals subdued.

text.p: Copper prices recovered on Friday's Bombay market helped by thin supplies and a rally in the world market along with speculation state-owned Hindustan Copper Ltd will hike selling prices, dealers said.
Other base metals showed little price movement.
Copper reopened strongly after Thursday's national holiday jumping 150 rupees to 12,750 rupees per quintal, more than making up the 50 rupees decline seen on Wednesday.
But traders said physical buying was low.
Stray physical buying kept tin and nickel steady.
Tin was steady at 34,400 rupees and nickel at 36,500 rupees per quintal. On Wednesday tin fell 200 rupees and nickel was down by 400 rupees per quintal.
Meanwhile aluminium was quiet at 7,250 rupees per quintal, as was zinc at 6,750 rupees and lead at 4,550 rupees per quintal amid nominal trading. --Bombay Commodities +91-22-265 9000
